_source: A significant number (plan 6.16). Doug, 2026-10-03: 'I thought that there might be number patterns for 7 and 12 as well. 12 tribes - 12 disciples. echo'; '12 seems real'; 'what about 12?'. Twelve counts SETS, not spans: the tribes, things numbered one for each tribe, the Twelve, and other sets the text counts. Every verse of the Berean with 'twelve' or '12' is placed on an occasion, quoted where the text ties one twelve to another, or set aside with its reason (complete: berean), checked by tools/numbers/significant_numbers.py. Revised the same day after the eight-reader review: 'sets beside', not 'ties'; Matthew's 'twelve thrones' not given as Luke's; the differing tribe lists said; Matthias (Acts 1:26) noted; Ishmael's twelve 'counted', not 'given'; the cloak's ten pieces and one tribe said.
name: twelve
lead: Twelve also counts years, cities, cubits and thousands. This card gathers the sets of twelve the text counts — the tribes, things numbered for the tribes, the Twelve — and the places where the text itself sets one twelve beside another.

phrases.match: one (man |leader )?(for|from) each tribe|thousand (men )?(were recruited )?from each tribe|thousand from each tribe|one from the leader of each tribe|one staff for the head of each tribe|From each of their fathers' tribes send one man|according to the number of the tribes
phrases.note: The text counts one from each tribe in places that do not say twelve (Num 1:4; 13:2; 34:18).

groups.title: The twelve tribes and Jacob's twelve sons
Other sets the text counts as twelve
groups.note: Listed because the text counts them; the text does not tie these to the tribes or to the Twelve.

occasions.title: Jacob's twelve sons
The twelve tribes of Israel
occasions.note: The text counts twelve tribes across lists that differ: Ezekiel gives Joseph two portions (47:13), and Revelation 7 names Levi and Joseph but not Dan or Ephraim.

occasions.title: Thrones, judging the twelve tribes
occasions.note: Matthew has twelve thrones; Luke has thrones. Matthew says 'you who have followed Me', Luke 'you who have stood by Me' (22:28); neither says 'the Twelve' here.

occasions.title: Twelve thousand sealed from each tribe
occasions.note: The tribes named here are Judah, Reuben, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph and Benjamin; Dan and Ephraim are not named. The text counts twelve tribes across lists that differ.

occasions.title: The city's twelve gates and twelve foundations
occasions.note: Rev 21:14 says 'the twelve apostles of the Lamb'; the card places them with the Twelve of the Gospels. The twelve foundation stones are named one by one (21:19-20).

occasions.title: Twelve pillars at the mountain
The breastpiece's twelve stones
The twelve leaders and their offerings
occasions.note: Each leader brings his tribe's offering on his own day (Num 7:12-83).

occasions.title: Twelve staffs
A thousand from each tribe against Midian
Twelve men sent to spy out the land
Twelve men and twelve stones at the Jordan
Ahijah's cloak torn in twelve pieces
occasions.note: Ten pieces for ten tribes, and one tribe kept 'for the sake of My servant David' (1 Kgs 11:31-32); the text does not say what each piece stands for.

occasions.title: Elijah's altar of twelve stones
Twelve goats and twelve bulls for all Israel
The Twelve
occasions.note: Linked to the events where the Twelve are chosen and sent; elsewhere they are named as a company. After Judas, Matthias is 'added to the eleven apostles' (Acts 1:26), a verse that does not say twelve.

occasions.title: Ishmael's twelve rulers
Twelve springs at Elim
Twelve loaves set before the LORD
Solomon's twelve governors
The Sea on twelve bronze oxen
Twelve lions on Solomon's steps
Elisha plowing with twelve teams of oxen
The Levite's concubine cut in twelve pieces
occasions.note: Sent 'throughout the territory of Israel'; the text does not say one for each tribe.

occasions.title: Twelve baskets left over
More than twelve legions of angels, which Jesus says He could ask for
A crown of twelve stars
The tree of life's twelve kinds of fruit

thousands.why: twelve thousand of an army, people or horses, or a measure of 12,000

years.why: years, months, days or hours, or an age. Jairus's daughter (twelve years old) and the woman who had bled twelve years share one story (Mark 5:21-43; Luke 8:40-56); Jesus was twelve at Passover (Luke 2:42)

counts.why: a count of cities, musicians, men or animals
